broadcasts.message: normalize.js implemented: NFKC, lowercase, collapse whitespace to single ASCII space, trim. No word changes. Ready for tokenizer and pipeline.
Tokenizer implemented: normalize then extract ASCII alphanumeric runs with interior apostrophes, preserving order and all tokens. No stopwords, negation preserved. Ready for integration.

Pipeline implemented: processText uses injected tokenize, returns exact shape. Frequencies uses null-prototype object to safely handle 'constructor'. Tokens and unique preserve order. No extra functions or hooks. Ready for integration.

private_memories.normalizer: Round 1: Task is to implement normalize.js. Requirements: apply NFKC, lowercase, collapse whitespace to one ASCII space, trim. Do not add/drop/replace/reorder words. Must handle string input only; for non-string? Spec says 'for string input', but host will pass strings. Use String.prototype.normalize('NFKC'). Then lowercase via toLowerCase(). Collapse whitespace: use regex /\s+/g replace with ' '. Trim. No shadowing of normalize. Keep function declaration top-level. No extra exports. Need to ensure no I/O, console. Ready to deliver.
private_memories.tokenizer: Round 1: I am implementing tokenizer.js per spec. It must call injected normalize(text), then extract ASCII alphanumeric runs with interior apostrophes, keeping order, no stopwords. I will rely on normalize.js for normalization. My file will only define tokenize function. Need to ensure no shadowing of normalize. I will use a regex with global flag and matchAll for safety, or match(). Will review in later rounds.
private_memories.integrator: Round 1: Initial implementation of pipeline.js. processText calls injected tokenize, returns {text, tokens, count, unique, frequencies}. Frequencies uses Object.create(null) to handle prototype keys like 'constructor'. text = tokens.join(' '). tokens preserved in order. unique preserves first-seen order. No shadowing of normalize/tokenize. Ready for review.
